newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says many Singaporeans working illegally.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says many Singaporeans working illegally.

text.p: Singaporeans comprised the largest number of professional and skilled workers who worked illegally in Malaysia last year, Malaysia Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayub said.

The Star newspaper on Saturday quoted Megat Junid as saying that workers from Malaysia's southern neighbour comprised 11,926 out of 21,926 skilled workers found to be in Malaysia without employment permits.
"They not only defied immigration laws but also skipped paying levy and income tax by working while on social visit passes," the Star quoted the minister as saying.
He added: "We have identified these people and will take action against them soon."
Megat Junid's comments follow a spate of sniping between Malaysia and Singapore government officials and newspapers.
Relations have been strained since late last year after Singapore senior statesman Lee Kuan Yew criticised Malaysia's southern Johor state.

Lee had said Johor, which is connected to Singapore by a causeway, was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" -- comments he later had deleted from the court affidavit in which they were contained.
As anger still simmered in Malaysia, the Singapore Straits Times in late April published stories that said Lee was probably justified in his criticisms about crime in Johor.
Malaysian newspapers in turn cited a United Nations report that crime in the city-state was higher than in Malaysia.
Megat Junid said the illegal Singaporean workers were employed as consultants for shipyards, factories and resorts.
The minister said Thais made up the second largest number of illegal skilled workers in Malaysia last year at 4,666, followed by Indonesians (551) and Japanese (478).
